brief: Barclays previews the September employment report. It forecasts +50k nonfarm and private payroll gains, putting the 3-month average at 78k, well above its roughly 0k/m breakeven pace, and sees the unemployment rate holding at 4.1%. That combination keeps the FOMC on hold at the October meeting before a 25bp hike in December. Forecast uncertainty is elevated: claims-based monthly models point to strong gains on recent momentum and weak initial claims, while alternative indicator models point to more modest gains. Barclays expects August's +162k to be revised down as BLS seasonal factors catch up: applying 2025's factors would have made it a 74k drop instead. A larger August revision down implies upside risk to the +50k September call. A small revision implies September comes in weaker. Average hourly earnings are forecast at +0.3% m/m (3.2% y/y) with the workweek down to 34.3 hours, implying payroll income growth cooled from August's spike. The payroll/household survey divergence persists and September won't resolve it. Separately, August JOLTS openings are forecast to slip to 7.2mn from 7.271mn, a level Barclays still views as overstating labor demand versus Indeed.com's weekly postings data.

cards.claim: Barclays forecasts 50k nonfarm payroll gains in September for both headline and private payrolls.

cards.anchor: We expect the unemployment rate to remain unchanged at 4.1%.

cards.claim: Nonfarm payrolls rose 31k in June, 21k in July and 162k in August.
cards.anchor: following gains in June (+31k), July (+21k) and August (+162k)

cards.claim: Barclays expects the FOMC to hold rates at its October meeting.
cards.anchor: this combination would keep an FOMC hold in play for the October meeting

cards.claim: Barclays expects the FOMC to proceed with a 25bp rate hike in December.
cards.anchor: before proceeding with a 25bp rate hike in December.

cards.claim: Barclays' monthly models, built from initial and continuing jobless claims data, project strong September payroll gains.
cards.anchor: Our usual monthly models — which work from weekly data on initial unemployment insurance claims, continuing claims, and other employment indicators — project strong gains

cards.claim: Barclays' alternative indicator models point to a return to more modest September job gains.
cards.anchor: the limited set of available indicators on hand pointing to a return to more modest job gains.

cards.claim: Barclays expects the seasonally adjusted August nonfarm payroll print to be revised down.
cards.anchor: We suspect that the seasonally adjusted August nonfarm payroll print will be revised down

cards.claim: Adjusted with 2025's seasonal factors, August nonfarm payrolls would have shown a 74k drop instead of the reported 162k gain.
cards.anchor: it would have registered a drop of 74k jobs instead of the 162k gain

cards.claim: A larger downward revision to August payrolls implies upside risk to Barclays' September payroll forecast.
cards.anchor: the more the August estimate gets revised down, the more the September estimate may appear strong, implying upside risks to our September payroll forecast

cards.claim: Little downward revision to August payrolls implies the September print comes in weaker than Barclays' 50k baseline.
cards.anchor: if the August estimates see little downward revision, we would expect the September payroll estimate to come in relatively weak, lower than our baseline forecast

cards.claim: Barclays forecasts average hourly earnings to rise 0.3% m/m and 3.2% y/y in September.
cards.anchor: We expect average hourly earnings to post a 0.3% m/m (3.2% y/y) rise in September

cards.claim: Barclays forecasts the average workweek to decline 0.1 hours to 34.3 hours in September.
cards.anchor: a decline in the workweek of 0.1hrs to 34.3hrs

cards.claim: Barclays expects private payroll income to have declined in September after its sharp August increase.
cards.anchor: September's estimates would likely show that private payroll income declined after its sharp increase in August.

cards.claim: The August unemployment rate ticked up from 4.090% to 4.141% despite a strong 162k job gain that month.
cards.anchor: a slight uptick in August's estimate, from 4.090% to 4.141% amid a month of strong job gains (+162k in August)

cards.claim: Barclays expects the divergence between payroll survey and household survey employment measures to persist.
cards.anchor: This reflects our view that the divergent measures from the payroll and household survey will persist.

cards.claim: Barclays' baseline is for the unemployment rate to trend lower through the end of 2026.
cards.anchor: We retain our baseline that the unemployment rate will trend lower through the end of 2026

cards.claim: Barclays forecasts August JOLTS job openings to decline to 7.200mn from 7.271mn.
cards.anchor: we think that job openings declined slightly, to 7.200mn from 7.271mn.

cards.claim: Barclays believes the current level of the JOLTS job openings survey overstates actual labor demand.
cards.anchor: signs from Indeed.com and other sources that the current level of JOLTS overstates labor demand.

cards.claim: Barclays regards Indeed.com's weekly job postings data as a much better indicator of the labor market's underlying trajectory than JOLTS.
cards.anchor: We regard the weekly estimates from Indeed.com — which are tabulated from job postings on its website — as a much-better indicator of the underlying trajectory.
